transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-03-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Luis (NimbleCart Eng Mgr), Priya (NimbleCart ML), Tara (Product)

Summary (auto): Live walkthrough of Hosted API chat/text generation basics and the Console Optimize suggestions for reducing cost and meeting latency SLOs.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, i'm maya from redwood, i'll do a quick intro and then hand over to connor for the deeper demo. can you all hear me ok?
[00:06] Luis: Yep, loud and clear. thanks maya.
[00:10] Maya: cool. nimblecart, just to confirm — your main use case is SKU summarization for product detail pages and a short customer chat assistant? maybe priya can add details.
[00:18] Priya: yeah that's right. mostly batch summarization from our nightly ingest and a small realtime chat that sits behind our help widget. latency is a big one for the chat — p50 targets around 300 to 350 ms, and we care a lot about per-token cost on the batch jobs.
[00:31] Maya: perfect, that's helpful. quick agenda: hosted api basics, streaming behavior demo, params you should tune, retries/idempotency, then a tour of the console sandbox and optimize recommendations.
[00:42] Connor: hi all, i'm connor, i'll jump into the sandbox in a minute — quick note, i might say 'k v cache' a few ways — sometimes it's k v cache, sometimes k-v cash, so apologies for my slop on acronyms.
[00:53] Tara: audible. no worries.
[00:55] [01:00] Connor: alright i'm sharing my screen — starting with a quick request flow. when you call the hosted chat endpoint you can stream partial tokens as they arrive. that reduces perceived latency by sending early tokens. so for the help widget scenario, streaming is usually what you want.
[01:15] Priya: does streaming chew up more connections? we have lots of small chats.
[01:20] Connor: good question — streaming keeps the request open, so you do hold an active connection per session, but the payload is smaller per chunk and you often finish faster. for many clients the overhead is lower because they can render progressively. we also expose a short polling fallback if you need connection pooling behavior.
[01:35] Luis: and how does that fit with retries? say a stream fails halfway. do we re-request with the same conversation state?
[01:42] Connor: so there are two patterns. best-effort: let the SDK retry from last known stable delta and append — that can lead to duplications if the server already emitted tokens. recommended: use idempotency tokens for non-streaming or short streaming with checkpoints. we also support partial KV/prefix caching — the runtime will cache prefix outputs for repeated prompts which helps a lot for FAQ-like items.
[02:03] Priya: prefix cache — is that something we control or automatic?
[02:06] Connor: currently automatic with opt-in per-route. you can set cache keys via the console or SDK metadata. on the console Optimize tab we'll show suggested TTLs based on traffic patterns.
[02:16] [02:30] Maya: i want to surface one quick tradeoff — when you enable aggressive batching and caching you save tokens, but you increase p99 because of batching waits. so for the chat widget you'd tune to small batches and streaming; for nightly summarization you'd use larger batches and quantized model variants to reduce cost.
[02:45] Tara: quantized model variants — do you host those for us or is that self-serve?
[02:49] Connor: we host the quantized variants in the hosted catalog; you can pick them in the model selector. for Dedicated or Private we provide the tooling and recommended artifacts to deploy.
[02:58] Luis: security question — we have PCI-adjacent data in product descriptions. what's the data retention and encryption story?
[03:04] Maya: we can share the SOC 2 and ISO docs — for hosted we support BYOK via KMS and all logs can be redacted on ingest, plus per-route retention in the console. i'll send the security packet after the call.
[03:15] Priya: perfect.
[03:18] [03:30] Connor: jumping into a live request — i'm going to make a short chat call with streaming turned on. watch the chunk events. (types) so you can see packets arriving every ~30ms in this demo because small tokens, but in your real traffic it varies with tokenization and model.
[03:46] Connor: note the SDK supports backpressure callbacks — if your UI can't keep up you can buffer or drop until you catch up. the SDK also exposes a "resume from token index" helper if you need to rehydrate after a reconnect.
[03:58] Priya: resume from token index — is that our thing to implement?
[04:02] Connor: the SDK exposes the helper; you supply the last acked token index and the server will stream the rest. it's not 100% atomic if you have side-effects in your prompt that rely on server state, which is why idempotency and checkpoints are important.
[04:15] Luis: ok. for the nightly batch jobs — you mentioned quantization and model selection. do you have cost delta numbers?
[04:22] Connor: rough numbers: a 4-bit quantized variant of a medium-sized gen model can be 2.5x cheaper per token at modest latency cost; for large seq lengths and heavy KV cache usage you might see smaller wins. Console Optimize will give a per-route cost estimate once you upload sample traffic.
[04:36] [04:45] Maya: i'm gonna show the new Optimize suggestions — connor, can you open the sample project i dropped into the sandbox?
[04:51] Connor: yep opening. (narration) the Optimize tab recommended: batch size 16 for nightly, prefix cache TTL 6 hours for product FAQ generation, enable streaming for chat routes, lower temperature to 0.2 for deterministic sku summaries, and set retry backoff to exponential with jitter starting at 150ms.
[05:13] Priya: the retry numbers — what about idempotency window? if we replay within 10s is it safe?
[05:18] Connor: our default idempotency window is 60s for hosted endpoints; you can configure shorter windows per-route. within 10s you're usually fine but we still recommend dedup logic client-side for the critical writes.
[05:29] Tara: can you show how to set the max tokens and top_p in the console?
[05:32] Connor: sure — model config, you set max_tokens, temperature, top_p. i'll demonstrate a small live change: reducing max_tokens from 512 to 200 on the chat route to limit cost for the widget.
[05:42] [05:55] Connor: making the change now — saved. now i'll run a synthetic request to show the latency delta. (runs) that request went from 420ms to 310ms p50, roughly. again this will vary with model and seq length.
[06:08] Luis: nice. is there a way to test multiple models quickly? like A/B?
[06:12] Connor: yes — rollouts in the console let you do canary and A/B with automatic traffic split and automatic fallback if the variant exceeds error thresholds. you can also tie rollouts to model version pins.
[06:24] Priya: error thresholds — how are those evaluated? is it only 5xx or also token-level hallucination metrics?
[06:29] Connor: we evaluate infra errors and performance SLAs automatically; for quality metrics like hallucination you can push evaluation sets and we'll alert on regression per route using your golden responses. that's part of the quality monitoring feature.
[06:41] [06:55] Maya: quick demo note: when streaming fails mid-response if you retry naively you can get duplicated text. recommended pattern is to use idempotency keys plus the resume helper, or re-request and diff against the last acked token.
[07:07] Priya: ok, practically speaking — what does the SDK surface for retries? is it configurable per call?
[07:12] Connor: yes, the SDK has retry policies you can set per call: max_retries, backoff_initial_ms, backoff_factor, jitter. there's also a convenience policy we recommend for chat with streaming. we'll attach the defaults in the quickstart.
[07:23] Luis: question on rate limits: if we burst a lot of small chats, do you throttle per-tenant or per-token?
[07:29] Connor: we do per-tenant concurrency limits and token throughput limits. for bursts we have a token bucket and you can apply client-side rate limiting. in Dedicated you can reserve capacity to avoid being throttled by shared limits.
[07:41] [07:55] Tara: how do logs show up? can we see token-level cost per-request?
[07:59] Maya: yes in the console billing view you'll see token breakdown per route and per-token cost estimates. we can also surface token counts in traces for debugging.
[08:10] Priya: great. can you walk through an edge case — suppose a user hits the widget and the stream starts, but the connection stalls for 20s then resumes; what's best practice?
[08:20] Connor: best practice: the client should use a short-lived heartbeat; if the connection stalls beyond the retry window, reconnect and call resume from the last acked token index. show a spinner in the UI and avoid re-sending prompts that mutate backend state. for server-side side-effects we recommend issuing the side-effect only when the response completes or using an explicit commit step.
[08:41] Luis: got it.
[08:44] [08:55] Connor: small demo of the SDK code — i'll paste an example (paraphrase): set idempotency_token = uuid(), set stream=true, register on_chunk callback, on_error retry with backoff. the SDK sample will be in the quickstart repo.
[09:09] Priya: can you include the resume helper in the repo?
[09:11] Connor: yes — it's in the SDK utilities folder.
[09:15] Maya: ok we're about halfway — any more product questions before i show the shared assets?
[09:20] Priya: one more — does Optimize ever suggest switching models mid-rollout automatically? like to a cheaper quantized one?
[09:25] Connor: Optimize will suggest candidate variants and cost/latency tradeoffs, but we don't automatically switch production traffic without your approval; you can enable automatic fallback only when certain infra conditions are met.
[09:36] [09:45] Maya: i'm going to drop links in chat now: sandbox project, quickstart repo, security packet, and a short bench script. Links: https://redwood.ai/sandbox/nimblecart, https://github.com/redwood-quickstarts/nimblecart-onramp, security: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2, bench: https://redwood.ai/bench/nimblecart-sample.
[09:59] Luis: thanks, i'll share with the infra team.
[10:02] Tara: will you include a list of recommended default parameters for our two routes (chat + batch)?
[10:07] Maya: yes i'll include a JSON config with recommended defaults — stream=true, temp=0.2, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=200 for chat; for batch: batch_size=16, quantized_model=true, prefix_cache_ttl=21600.
[10:18] [10:30] Priya: about observability — can we get traces correlated to our request IDs?
[10:33] Connor: yes pass client_request_id and we will show traces correlated in the console tracing tab, plus error traces.
[10:39] Luis: any notes on regional routing? we need EU data residency for some customers.
[10:43] Maya: we have EU regions in hosted; you can pin routes to region in the console or use Private for strict residency. i'll note to include region mapping in the follow-up.
[10:54] [11:05] Priya: small nit — when SDKs reconnect they sometimes replay events and our UI double-renders. you said resume helpers but is there an example debounce pattern?
[11:12] Connor: yes the UI sample demonstrates a dedupe de-dup token buffer that ignores duplicate token ids for 200ms windows. i'll put that in the repo.
[11:22] Tara: how are model upgrades handled? we have concerns about subtle behavior changes.
[11:27] Connor: we recommend pinning model versions and using the rollout canary with eval sets. Console will run regression alerts if your golden set diverges by a threshold and you can auto-roll back.
[11:39] [11:50] Maya: wrapping up — recap of next steps: we'll send sandbox + repo + security docs, connor will share bench script and optimize screenshot, nimblecart to send sample prompts and pick pilot metrics.
[11:59] Luis: sounds good. can we get an estimated cost ballpark for the pilot?
[12:04] Maya: i'll include a back-of-envelope in the follow-up based on your sample traffic if you upload it to the sandbox.
[12:10] Priya: thanks, this was helpful.
[12:13] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up by friday. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: some acronyms transcribed inconsistently (e.g., KV cache as "k v cache"), occasional filler words and brief crosstalk.
